newsitem.title: JAPAN: Big Japan banks reveal BIS ratios, latent profits.
newsitem.headline: Big Japan banks reveal BIS ratios, latent profits.

text.p: Japan's 10 commercial "city" banks said on Friday their preliminary international capital adequacy ratios at the end of the fiscal half-year on September 30 were as follows, with comparisons from the previous six-month period:
Under the rules of the Bank for International Settlements (BIS), Japanese banks operating internationally need to have capital equivalent to eight percent of risk-weighted assets.
Unlike many countries, Japanese authorities allow banks to include unrealised profits on securities holdings as part of capital.
Unrealised profits on securities holdings are as follows (in billions of yen unless stated, with previous six-month comparisons):

The full names of the banks are: Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd, Sumitomo Bank Ltd, Sanwa Bank Ltd, Sakura Bank Ltd, Fuji Bank Ltd, Tokai Bank Ltd, Asahi Bank Ltd, Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi Ltd, Daiwa Bank Ltd and Hokkaido Takushoku Bank Ltd.

BOT-Mitsubishi was formed in April 1996 through a merger between Mitsubishi Bank Ltd and Bank of Tokyo Ltd. The comparison data for the bank is calculated by combining figures from the two former banks.
